clue.text: Satisfied with debts, but unlikely to reach agreement

parts.note: satisfied means content
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: A creditor is happy with what is owed but expects no settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A contentious person or issue provokes argument, so agreement is unlikely; a descriptive paraphrase.

clue.text: One applauds the bell-ringer

definitions.meaning: someone who claps hands in approval
the tongue inside a bell that strikes it and makes it ring

explanation.surface: Someone cheers the person ringing the church bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bell-ringer' suggests a person; it is the metal piece that swings inside the bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a person who claps, and the striking tongue of a bell.

clue.text: No way to get in — that's bad

indicators.note: one piece is told to get in, i.e. to go inside the other

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A refusal to let someone enter, described as a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and bad are synonyms, both meaning unpleasant or harmful.

clue.text: Wastes time, a case for improvement

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are to be bettered by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone squanders time on a case that needs work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wastes' reads as a verb about time, and it is: in the sense of making thin, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To waste someone is to make them thin and feeble, the sense of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Bite from climbing insect

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small insect

explanation.surface: An insect crawling up someone gives them a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Bite is a sharp, pungent taste; tang is a synonym for that sharpness.

clue.text: Terrible crooner died, it's official

indicators.note: a terrible rendering of the word suggests its letters are mangled

explanation.surface: It is now formally confirmed that an awful singer has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stated publicly and formally documented is official; an idiom for formal acknowledgement.

clue.text: Good man and bad coming together, nevertheless

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Even so, good and bad people end up together.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, the word means even so or nonetheless, a synonym.

clue.text: Maintained member has got into crooked deal

indicators.note: the limb is said to get into the other piece, so it goes inside
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a member has become involved in a corrupt deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintained' looks like kept up, but it means claimed. 'crooked' gives ALED from the deal, and 'has got into' puts the limb inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to assert it, as alleged claims are asserted without proof.

clue.text: Almost a full month before beds will bear fruit

indicators.note: one piece is placed before the other in the answer
almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: April is one complete month of the year
cots are small beds

explanation.surface: Within a month or so, the garden beds will produce fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: These small orange stone fruits are an example of fruit.

clue.text: Spilled Brian's tea — he won't have a drink

indicators.note: spilled tea is scattered, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the name with its possessive S, all used as letters

explanation.surface: Brian's tea is knocked over, and a teetotaller explains himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains, especially from alcohol, refuses drinks; a description of a teetotaller.

clue.text: Mischievous person joins the Spanish force

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or sprite
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A troublemaker signs up with a Spanish military force.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone to act is to drive or urge them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: In radiography, sickness is given a cure

indicators.note: the letters sit in the words that follow, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: An X-ray reveals an illness, which is then treated.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for medicine, a remedy or cure.

clue.text: Hair-raising action by the brave

parts.note: hair-raising means terrifying, but read literally it is lifting hair off a head, as a warrior (a brave) once did

explanation.surface: A terrifying feat performed by a courageous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' is a noun here, an old term for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the skin and hair of the head as a trophy literally raises hair.

clue.text: Go round to add note to list

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An instruction to circulate and add a note to a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn about an axis is to go round, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stylish set with fault needs fixing

indicators.note: the letters need to be put right, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A smart set with a defect needs to be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing good taste and elegance means stylish, a synonym.

clue.text: Title that's used in all-in wrestling?

definitions.text: Title that's used in all-in wrestling?

parts.words: Title that's used in all-in wrestling?
parts.note: the legal title to own land outright, read as a grip that is unrestricted, as in a no-holds-barred bout

explanation.surface: A question about championship belts in freestyle wrestling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' suggests a championship; it is a legal title to property.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright, permanent ownership of land is a form of legal title.

clue.text: Artificial language providing neat prose

indicators.note: something artificial is made up, so these letters are made up into a new word

explanation.surface: An invented tongue that yields elegant writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artificial' does double service: it signals the rearrangement and also describes this constructed tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the best-known constructed international tongue, an example of a language.

clue.text: Instructor is oddly curt, intercepting suggestive look

indicators.note: one piece intercepts the other, cutting into its middle

parts.note: a leer is a lewd, suggestive look

indicators.note: the word curt is treated oddly, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A teacher curtly interrupts someone's leering glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a pick of odd letters, but here it jumbles all four letters to CTUR, and 'intercepting' splits the look after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A university teacher who gives talks is an instructor, a synonym.

clue.text: Helped fool with nutty diets

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Someone foolish was aided by eccentric eating plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nutty' turns DIETS into ISTED; nuts on a diet make a neat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assisted is to have been helped, matching past tense.

clue.text: It may have to be paid after a union dispute is settled

definitions.text: It may have to be paid after a union dispute is settled

parts.words: It may have to be paid after a union dispute is settled
parts.note: a union suggests a trade union, but here it is a marriage, and the dispute settled is a divorce

explanation.surface: Back pay owed once a trade union's strike is resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' points to trade unions; it means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to a former spouse after divorce settlement; the clue describes it.

clue.text: Fits sergeant-major into health resorts

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: spas are health resorts

explanation.surface: A sergeant-major is squeezed into a holiday at spa towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden convulsions or seizures are fits, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Officer shortly to penetrate clear harbour

indicators.note: one piece penetrates the other, going inside

parts.note: sheer fabric is clear, see-through
LT is the short form of lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer briefly gets into a clear harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' sounds like a noun for ships; here it is the verb sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour is to give refuge or protection, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: It's on the cards it may precede crisis

definitions.meaning: what an ID card shows: who you are
the word that comes before crisis in the phrase for doubt about who one is

explanation.surface: A prediction that something likely is about to come to a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the cards' means likely, but here it is literally printed on cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Who someone is appears on ID cards, and the same word forms the phrase for a personal crisis.

clue.text: Secure link

definitions.meaning: to fasten, as by binding with rope
a connection or partnership between two things

explanation.surface: A safe connection.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means fasten securely; as a noun, a connection or tie.

clue.text: People will mind if you dump your kids here

definitions.text: People will mind if you dump your kids here

parts.words: People will mind if you dump your kids here
parts.note: mind seems to mean object, but here it means look after children

explanation.surface: A warning that others will be annoyed if you abandon your children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mind' reads as take offence, but means look after.
explanation.definitionFit: A day nursery where staff look after young children while parents are away.

clue.text: Title-holder takes tea with politician

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A champion sits down for tea with a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for champion, someone holding a sporting title.

clue.text: Opening with a key, it is essential

parts.note: D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A key opens it, which is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance passage into a mine is an opening.

clue.text: Round safety device that's practicable

parts.note: O is round in shape
a fuse is an electrical safety device

explanation.surface: A circular safety device that actually works.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable or helpful is practicable, the phrase meaning useful.

clue.text: Communist and German worker no longer needed

parts.note: Red is a common term for a communist
und is German for and
a worker ant is the commonest kind of ant

explanation.surface: A communist and a German worker are both laid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Made jobless because the role is surplus, the employment sense.

clue.text: A jumper that rides up!

parts.note: a jumper seems a sweater riding up the body; it is a person who jumps and rides up in an aircraft first

explanation.surface: A complaint about a sweater that creeps up the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a British sweater; it is someone who jumps from aircraft, flown up first.
explanation.definitionFit: An airborne soldier who jumps from aircraft by parachute after being flown up.
